As we wrap up, just take a moment to reflect on the journey you’ve just taken. If you’ve stuck with this story, you’ve seen how one life—shaped by love, loss, and the constant search for dignity—can actually spark a movement that changes everything. “When They Call You a Terrorist” isn’t just about one person, or one moment in time. It’s really about how regular people, just like you and me, can demand extraordinary change, even when the odds feel impossible.
So, as you move forward, here are a few things worth carrying with you:
Real change? It starts with honest storytelling and the courage to let yourself be seen. Taking care of your community—and yourself—is just as important as showing up to protest. Progress can be slow, uneven, sometimes even invisible, but every step you take matters. Art, culture, and your unique voice are powerful tools for reclaiming hope and dignity. And remember, fighting for justice isn’t a sprint—it’s a marathon. Give yourself permission to rest and recharge along the way.
Here’s what this really means for you: The work of justice? It’s not just for a chosen few. It belongs to all of us—in the choices we make, the stories we share, and the care we show to each other. You don’t have to be perfect or fearless to make a difference. You just have to begin—right where you are, with what you have, and with the people around you.
The world won’t change overnight. But every act of love, every honest moment, every time you refuse to accept injustice—you’re moving us closer to the world we all deserve. So, carry that torch forward. Know that you’re not alone, and your story can be the spark that lights up real change.
